summary: Iran has halted routine IAEA inspections at its nuclear facilities until US military threats cease, while Israeli intelligence reports Iran planning drone attacks against Trump and senior US officials. Hamas confirms its Rafah Brigade commander killed in an Israeli airstrike in southern Gaza. Six Gulf states demanded Iranian compensation for missile and UAV attacks at the UN Security Council.
key_points: Iran announces suspension of routine IAEA inspections at nuclear facilities, demanding discussion of consequences of strikes on its nuclear sites (Source: @yediotnews25/137815).

Mossad passed CIA intelligence that Iran plans drone attacks against Trump and senior US officials, verified by another Western agency; US officials moved to secure facilities (Source: @yediotnews25/137812).
Hamas confirms Rafah Brigade commander Samir Abu Younis (Abu Mahmoud) killed in Israeli airstrike in southern Gaza; veteran since 1991, involved in Oct 7 planning (Source: @manniefabian/59518).

Six Gulf states (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman) demand Iranian compensation for missile and UAV attacks since Feb 28 at UN Security Council; Iran accuses them of assisting US strikes (Source: @yediotnews25/137804).
Saudi air defenses intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh; debris fell near Mecca at Sabuhah and Wadi al-Maghmas (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10045).
Israeli artillery struck 44 locations across southern Lebanon on Nov 14, 2026, with 5 air strikes and 50 drone sightings recorded (Source: @redlinkleb/53270).
Trump reportedly told Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Oct 31 he plans to attack Iran after US midterms; MBS urged against it citing sanctions effectiveness (Source: @yediotnews25/137805).
Iran launched UAV from Omidiyeh Air Base in Khuzestan and conducted missile launch toward Strait of Hormuz from Hormozgan (Source: @shin_persian/12367, @shin_persian/12358).

sections.executive_summary: Iran has halted routine IAEA inspections at its nuclear facilities until US military threats cease, while Israeli intelligence reports Iran planning drone attacks against Trump and senior US officials. Hamas confirms its Rafah Brigade commander killed in an Israeli airstrike in southern Gaza. Six Gulf states demanded Iranian compensation for missile and UAV attacks at the UN Security Council.

points: Iran announced the suspension of routine IAEA inspections at its nuclear facilities, stating inspections will not resume while US military threats continue, and demanded discussions on consequences of strikes on nuclear sites (Source: @yediotnews25/137815).

Israeli intelligence (Mossad) provided CIA with specific intelligence on Iranian plans to launch drone attacks against President Trump and senior US officials, verified by another Western agency; US officials relocated to secure facilities and Trump's public appearances reduced (Source: @yediotnews25/137812).
A UAV was launched from Omidiyeh Air Base in Khuzestan Province, Iran, as detected by monitoring systems (Source: @shin_persian/12367).
UAV activity was observed over Jolfa and Hadishahr in East Azerbaijan Province, Iran (Source: @shin_persian/12359).
A missile launch toward the Strait of Hormuz was detected from Hormozgan Province, Iran, and blasts were subsequently heard in the Strait (Source: @shin_persian/12358, @shin_persian/12365).

Six Gulf Cooperation Council states formally demanded Iranian compensation for damages from missile and UAV attacks on their territories since February 28, presenting the demand at the UN Security Council; Iran countered by accusing Gulf states of assisting US strikes against Iran (Source: @yediotnews25/137804).

Trump reportedly informed Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on October 31 of plans to attack Iran after US midterm elections; MBS urged restraint, citing sanctions effectiveness (Source: @yediotnews25/137805).

Prime Minister Netanyahu attempted to contact Haredi leader Moti Babchik (representing the Ger Rebbe) for meetings, but Babchik did not respond; Likud denies the report (Source: @yediotnews25/137813).

Netanyahu wrote to opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot proposing to enter negotiations without preconditions to reach agreements on security and the draft law, including with Haredi representatives (Source: @yediotnews25/137809, @amitsegal/67197).
Eisenkot dismissed Netanyahu's statement as a spin, noting a negotiation meeting between Yashar! and Likud teams was already scheduled for the next day (Source: @amitsegal/67200).
Israeli warplanes were active in the south, as indicated by live mapping (Source: @redlinkleb/53275).

Israeli artillery conducted shelling at multiple locations in southern Lebanon: Zibqin, Wadi al-Saluqi, Wadi al-Hujeir, Wadi Nahla, and dropped illumination bombs over Shama and Majdal Zoun (Source: @redlinkleb/53274, @redlinkleb/53254, @redlinkleb/53280, @redlinkleb/53258, @redlinkleb/53259, @redlinkleb/53261).

Daily statistics for November 14, 2026 show 142 total alerts, 50 drone sightings (most in Bint Jbeil area), 5 air strikes (Aita al-Jabal, Al-Zut, Kfar Tibnit, Wadi al-Hujeir, Al-Qantara), and artillery shelling at 44 locations across southern Lebanon (Source: @redlinkleb/53270).

Israeli Border Police officer fired at a vehicle on Highway 85 after the driver endangered pedestrians and the officer; driver fled and was hospitalized in serious condition (Source: @N12chat/235075).

Hamas confirmed its Rafah Brigade commander Samir Abu Younis (Abu Mahmoud) was killed in an Israeli airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip overnight; he was a veteran commander since 1991 and involved in planning the October 7 attack (Source: @manniefabian/59518).

The IDF struck a senior Hamas military wing commander in the Khan Younis area; Hamas identified the target as the Rafah Brigade commander, though the IDF has not yet confirmed the kill (Source: @manniefabian/59518).

Previous Rafah Brigade commanders were killed: Nael Abu Obeid (Abu Atiya) in September 2025, and Muhammad Shabana on May 13, 2025, in a strike on a hospital that also killed Hamas leader Mohammad Sinwar (Source: @manniefabian/59518, @N12chat/235073).
The IDF conducted a strike on the Nasser Hospital complex in Khan Younis on Thursday targeting the commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade (Source: @manniefabian/59518).

Shas party rejected MK Pindrus's suggestion that Shas would not oppose a draft solution, stating Shas does not negotiate with any faction in the left-wing coalition per the Council of Torah Sages (Source: @yediotnews25/137810).

Israeli artillery shelling hit multiple locations in southern Lebanon on November 14, 2026: Zibqin, Wadi al-Saluqi, Wadi al-Hujeir, Wadi Nahla, with illumination bombs dropped over Shama and Majdal Zoun (Source: @redlinkleb/53274, @redlinkleb/53254, @redlinkleb/53280, @redlinkleb/53258, @redlinkleb/53259, @redlinkleb/53261).

Daily alert report for November 14, 2026 recorded 142 total alerts, 50 drone sightings (highest in Bint Jbeil district with 6 sightings at Al-Burj Al-Shamali, 4 at Qana, 3 at Meidoun), 5 air strikes (Aita al-Jabal, Al-Zut 2, Kfar Tibnit, Wadi al-Hujeir, Al-Qantara), and artillery shelling at 44 distinct locations across Tyre, Bint Jbeil, and Marjayoun districts (Source: @redlinkleb/53270).
A UNIFIL helicopter conducted a medical evacuation from its headquarters in Naqoura to Beirut; Lebanese authorities advised residents not to panic (Source: @redlinkleb/53272).
No specific operational developments in Syria or Iraq were reported in the provided messages.

Six Gulf states (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman) demanded Iranian compensation for damages from missile and UAV attacks on their territories since February 28, presented by GCC Secretary General Jasem Al-Budaiwi at the UN Security Council (Source: @yediotnews25/137804).

Saudi air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Houthis from Yemen toward Riyadh; debris fell near Mecca at Sabuhah and Wadi al-Maghmas; Houthis deny targeting holy cities (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10045, @N12chat/235084).
Bahrain activated an alert for a "possible threat" (Source: @N12chat/235083).

Trump reportedly told Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on October 31 he plans to attack Iran after US midterm elections; MBS urged against it, citing sanctions effectiveness (Source: @yediotnews25/137805).

sections.threat_assessment: Iran's suspension of IAEA inspections and reported drone threats against US leadership signal a significant escalation in nuclear and asymmetric warfare risks. The killing of Hamas's Rafah Brigade commander degrades command continuity but may not disrupt operations given rapid replacements. Israeli artillery intensity in southern Lebanon remains high, with 44 shelling locations in a single day, indicating sustained pressure on Hezbollah. Houthi missile attacks on Saudi Arabia persist despite interceptions, threatening regional energy infrastructure and holy sites. The convergence of Iranian nuclear brinkmanship, proxy attacks, and Israeli military operations creates a multi-front escalation ladder with limited off-ramps.
sections.regional_response: Gulf states have formalized demands for Iranian compensation at the UN Security Council, framing Iranian missile and UAV attacks as violations of sovereignty. Saudi Arabia demonstrates effective missile defense but faces continued Houthi pressure. Bahrain's threat alert reflects heightened Gulf anxiety. Iran's counter-accusation of Gulf complicity in US strikes hardens regional divisions. The reported Trump-MBS conversation suggests potential US military action against Iran post-midterms, which could dramatically alter regional calculus. Arab states appear to be coordinating diplomatic pressure while preparing for possible conflict expansion.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Mossad-CIA intelligence sharing on Iranian drone plots against US officials represents a high-confidence, actionable threat that has already prompted protective measures. Iranian UAV launches from Omidiyeh and missile tests toward the Strait of Hormuz indicate operational readiness for maritime and aerial strikes. The daily Lebanese alert data provides granular pattern-of-life intelligence on Israeli targeting priorities. Hamas's rapid commander replacement cycle (three Rafah Brigade commanders in six months) suggests resilient command structures despite decapitation strikes. The UNSC compensation demand creates a legal-diplomatic track that could precede broader sanctions or coalition action.
